perf.summary: Vectorize the GF(2) row XOR (a[r*m+j] ^= a[pivot*m+j]) over wider words; it is the inner hot loop and is trivially SIMD-able.
perf.currentCost: The inner 'for j: a[r*m+j] ^= a[pivot*m+j]' runs over the full width m for every eliminated row, giving O(n*m) int XORs per pivot and O(rank*n*m) overall. As written, int-at-a-time XOR is one operation per 4 bytes; Burst can auto-vectorize but the row-major int layout wastes 31/32 of each int when the matrix is over GF(2) (entries are 0/1).
perf.proposedChange: Hoist the row base pointers out of the inner loop: int* rowR = a + r*m; int* rowP = a + pivotRow*m; then loop 'rowR[j] ^= rowP[j]'. This removes the repeated r*m and pivotRow*m multiplies/address computations from every iteration and gives Burst a clean two-pointer XOR loop it vectorizes cleanly. Higher-impact (separate, larger-API change): pack GF(2) rows as bitsets (ulong words, m/64 words) so each XOR processes 64 entries at once, cutting the inner loop length by 64x and shrinking RAM 32x.
perf.rationale: Pointer hoisting removes two integer multiplies and an add from the address calculation of every inner iteration, shortening the address-gen dependency chain and helping the vectorizer prove contiguity. The bitset packing is an asymptotic constant-factor win (64x fewer word ops, 32x less memory, far fewer cache lines touched) — decisive for large matroids.
perf.risk: Pointer hoisting is purely semantics-preserving. The bitset repacking changes the public matrix representation (a[] layout and the basis/Rank contract) and the FindPivotRow/SwapRows code, so it is an API-level change, not a drop-in; flag as a larger refactor. Both keep GF(2) XOR semantics identical.

perf.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the tiny leaf helpers (FindPivotRow, SwapRows, EliminateOtherRows) and drop the unused 'using' directives.
perf.currentCost: FindPivotRow, SwapRows, EliminateOtherRows are private leaf helpers called inside the column loop. Without an inlining hint the JIT/Burst may keep call overhead (frame setup, parameter marshaling of the many int args). Also 'using System;' is unused in both files and System.Runtime.CompilerServices is unused unless attributes are added.
perf.proposedChange: Annotate the three private helpers with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] so the hot column loop inlines them and the compiler can keep n,m,a in registers across the merged body, exposing the inner XOR/pivot loops to fusion. Remove the unused 'using System;'.
perf.rationale: Inlining these small, frequently-called helpers removes call overhead and lets the optimizer hoist invariants (e.g., a+pivotRow*m) across what are currently separate function boundaries. Burst already inlines aggressively, so impact is low, but the hint is free and the using cleanup reduces noise.
perf.risk: Inlining a leaf with two nested loops (EliminateOtherRows) can grow code size; Burst may already do this. Purely a hint — no semantic change. Removing an unused using is safe.
